must_read.title: Effects of Maternal Ligature-Induced Periodontitis on Brain in Offspring
must_read.abstract: The combined effects of chronic maternal periodontitis on offspring gut microbiome and brain outcomes remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of maternal oral microbiome disruption on brain function and gut microbiome in offspring. Periodontitis was induced in 11- to 12-wk-old parous C57BL/6J mice by maintaining ligatures around both sides of the maxillary second molars for 4 wk, followed by breeding with naïve male mice. Maternal oral and gut microbiome, as well as the offspring gut microbiome, was analyzed by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Male offspring were evaluated at 7 to 8 wk of age via a set of analyses, including behavioral tests, microbiome profiling, RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry for glial cell populations, and in vivo calcium imaging. Cerebellar DNA methylation was assessed at embryonic day 18.5 to examine early epigenetic alterations. Maternal periodontitis significantly reduced microbial diversity in the maternal oral microbiome and altered the composition of the maternal gut microbiome. In offspring, α-diversity was reduced in the gut microbiome. Behavioral analyses revealed impaired social interaction and reduced spontaneous locomotion, while motor coordination and memory-related behaviors were preserved. RNA sequencing identified region-specific changes in gene expression, particularly in the cerebellum, highlighting its vulnerability to maternal inflammatory conditions. DNA methylation analysis revealed epigenetic alterations during the fetal stage, suggesting early programming effects. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated a significant increase in astrocyte density in the cerebellum and frontal cortex, whereas oligodendrocytes and microglia were unaffected. Furthermore, calcium imaging revealed disrupted neuronal synchrony among Purkinje cells without significant changes in individual neuronal activity parameters. Maternal oral microbiome disruption induces coordinated alterations in maternal and offspring microbiomes and leads to persistent neurobehavioral, molecular, and cellular changes in offspring. These findings provide new insights into the link between maternal oral health and offspring neurodevelopment, highlighting the potential role of microbiome-mediated mechanisms in shaping brain function.

scan.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics
scan.domain: 生物材料表面/降解产物如…
scan.cluster: 生物材料表面/降解产物如…
scan.abstract: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. Well-defined internal cavities and engineerable interior and exterior surfaces enable the spatial organization of therapeutic cargoes, molecular recognition elements, and bioactive components within a single nanoscale platform. In this Review, we examine the structural organization, self-assembly mechanisms, physicochemical properties, and functional diversity of representative protein nanocages, including ferritin, the pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 core, DNA-binding proteins from starved cells (Dps), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), encapsulins, and lumazine synthase. We discuss how their structural features and assembly behavior govern biological performance and support biomedical applications in targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and in vivo and in vitro diagnostics. Beyond describing individual platforms, we establish a unifying framework that positions protein nanocages as programmable molecular organizers and highlights five transferable design principles: multivalent ligand display, spatial compartmentalization, receptor-guided targeting, reporter organization and signal enhancement, and stimulus-responsive cargo release and functional activation. We also examine persistent challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation, alongside emerging opportunities in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational protein design. Collectively, these principles establish protein nanocages as versatile biomaterial platforms for integrating sensing, targeting, imaging, and therapy within a single molecular architecture, providing a foundation for next-generation precision nanomedicine. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Reviews typically treat protein nanocages individually, obscuring shared structural features and the extent to which design strategies transfer across systems. This Review addresses this gap by establishing a comparative framework spanning structurally diverse nanocages and distilling their similarities into a concise set of generalizable design principles. scan.title: Metronomic Tegafur-Uracil Maintenance Therapy in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Following Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy
scan.domain: 口腔鳞癌的免疫微环境与微…
scan.cluster: 口腔鳞癌的免疫微环境与微…
scan.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) is the predominant subtype of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan. Despite the guideline-recommended adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for advanced pathological risk factors, long-term survival remains suboptimal. We evaluated the efficacy of tegafur-uracil as metronomic maintenance therapy following adjuvant CRT. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study analyzed 197 OCSCC patients who underwent curative resection followed by adjuvant CRT. Patients were stratified by receipt of metronomic tegafur-uracil maintenance therapy. Survival outcomes were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: Patients receiving metronomic maintenance therapy (49.2%, 97/197) demonstrated favorable survival trends compared with those who did not. Five-year disease-free survival and disease-specific survival rates were 57.4% vs. 53.0% (p = 0.101), and 70.1% versus 60.8% (p = 0.092), respectively. Patients with ≥ 2 risk factors-extreme body mass index, positive margins, extranodal extension, and advanced depth of invasion-demonstrated significantly better outcomes following metronomic maintenance therapy. Therapy initiation at 1-3 months post-CRT and a treatment duration exceeding 12 months were also associated with a better prognosis. CONCLUSION: Metronomic tegafur-uracil maintenance therapy was associated with favorable outcomes, particularly in patients presenting with ≥ 2 identified risk factors. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

scan.title: Immediate Implants With or Without a Volume Stable Collagen Matrix: A Randomized Clinical Trial
scan.abstract: AIM: This randomized clinical trial evaluated soft tissue thickness (STT) around immediate implants with or without soft tissue augmentation using a volume-stable collagen matrix (VCMX). Secondary outcomes included clinical, esthetic, volumetric, and patient-reported outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Participants received immediate implants in the anterior esthetic zone with (Test) or without (Control) simultaneous VCMX augmentation. Outcomes were assessed before surgery, immediately after surgery, and at 6 and 12 months. The primary outcome was STT. Within- and between-group comparisons were performed using the Friedman rank test and Mann-Whitney U test, respectively. Secondary outcomes included mucosal level (ML), marginal bone level (MBL), esthetic and patient-reported outcomes, and volumetric changes. RESULTS: Thirty-eight out of 40 patients completed the study. STT was significantly greater in the Test group at all follow-ups (p < 0.05). At 12 months, STT in the Test group increased significantly at 3 mm from the gingival margin (1.85 mm, SE 0.19, p < 0.0001) and non-significantly at 6 mm (1.29 mm, SE 0.24, p = 0.0917), whereas STT in the Control group decreased non-significantly at 3 mm (0.18 mm, SE 0.18, p = 0.6213) and at 6 mm (0.36 mm, SE 0.10, p = 0.1054). ML remained stable in the Test group but showed significant recession in the Control group. Selected esthetic and patient-reported outcomes favored the Test group. MBL did not change significantly over time in either group. Volumetric analysis showed no significant change over time in the Test group, whereas the Control group showed significant shrinkage (p = 0.0201). CONCLUSIONS: VCMX augmentation may improve soft tissue stability around immediate implants. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study protocol was registered on September 20, 2021 in the ClinicalTrials.gov database (registration number: NCT05081284).
